newsitem.title: USA: Seven Caribbean airlines discuss cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Seven Caribbean airlines discuss cooperation pact.

text.p: Seven Caribbean airlines are in talks over possible cooperative agreements that could make them more efficient for both cargo and passenger operations, a chief executive of one of the airlines involved said.
"We don't know what form this might take," Gilles Filliatreault, president and chief executive of British West Indies Airways (BWIA), told Reuters.
"We are meeting now and identifying issues. We hope to establish an action plan," he said. "We hope to have something in some form in two months."

The chief executives of the seven Caribbean airlines met over the weekend in Miami. They were in town to attend the International Airline CEO Conference organized by the Aviation and Latin America & Caribbean newsletter.

Many smaller airlines are reeling under competitive pressures from giants such as AMR Corp's American Airlines. That pressure will only increase if proposed alliances between big airlines -- such as American and British Airways -- are approved.

Some of the world's smaller airlines are striking their own alliances with these big competitors, such as the TACA group of Central America's proposal to ally with American. The Caribbean group could take another tack with a group agreement.
Aviation consultant Robert said:"BWIA and Air Jamaica have taken lead. The other airlines in the talks are Bahamasair, ALM Antillean Airlines, Air Aruba, Surinam Airways and Guyana Airways.
Issues under study include aircraft leasing, cargo sales and handling, fuel purchasing and other topics. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
